info.desc: Purple is the second album released by the American rock band Stone Temple Pilots, on June 7, 1994, by Atlantic Records. It contains several of the band's biggest hit songs, including "Vasoline," "Interstate Love Song," and "Big Empty," which was also featured on The Crow soundtrack. The album was a big success for STP, debuting at #1 (for three weeks, longer than any stay at the top by Nirvana, Alice In Chains, or Soundgarden) and being certified 6x platinum. In 2006, the album was ranked number 73 on Guitar World magazine's list of the greatest 100 guitar albums of all .

podcast.body: "Purple" debuted at number one on the charts in the US, also reaching number one in Australia, number two in Canada, and number ten in the UK, indicating significant international success. "Hype was such that the album debuted at number one on the charts in the US, and made it as high as number one in Australia, number two in Canada, number ten in the UK."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Recorded in Atlanta during a break in the band's touring schedule, this album was completed rather quickly in four weeks, partly due to Scott Wyland's drug use allowing him to avoid withdrawal symptoms. Released on June 7, 1994, it showcased a sound that was "less grunge and more straight ahead all rock" compared to their debut. "Purple was released on June 7th, 1994, and I remember when it came out thinking, wow, this sounds a lot different than the first album."

podcast.body: This is the band's second album and contains a hidden track at the end, which is not performed by the Stone Temple Pilots themselves. The final listed song, "Kitchenware and Candybars," is notably long at 8 minutes and 6 seconds, serving as an indicator that additional audio might be present. The hidden track, "My Second Album," is a comedic piece by band friend Richard Peterson, designed to mock other bands' use of hidden tracks. "That's their second album, which, as you'll soon see, is a very important and salient fact."
